findings.title: R1 validates a snapshot then rereads the caller-controlled mapping
findings.argument: The public frozen dataclass accepts entries of arbitrary type. check_pinned_margins copies two values and validates them, but lookup returns self.entries[key] again. A dict subclass returning pinned floats for the validation reads and 0.0 on the next read returns an unpinned zero margin. packed_attention repeats validation but also reaches its recording packed_run with e_q=0, delta=0 at epsilon=1 (five mapping reads). No product monkeypatch or dataclass mutation used. Ordinary loaded tables are immutable and safe; this gap is hand-built mapping provenance/TOCTOU.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the validated immutable snapshot (or canonical pinned value) for lookup; normalize public construction to a private immutable copy. Do not reread untrusted mapping values after checking them.
findings.prior_art: TOCTOU / CWE-367, unverified -- lead to check: CWE-367 check use snapshot; SHA-256 NIST FIPS180-4 (2015). No new technique.
findings.status: confirmed CPU host bypass; no GPU required

findings.title: D12 finite squared-norm overflow still hides a dense non-finite row
findings.argument: D64, seed42/KV1 tables, all finite k[bad,0]=float32(1e20), other coordinates zero, q=-ones. Sequential fp32 v*v makes ss=Inf, norm=Inf, unit=0, all codes=8. Packed coefficient=-0.0803470984, score=-Inf, so the key is skipped beside zero keys. Dense reconstruction (CB[8] @ R)*Inf has 31 +Inf and 33 -Inf coordinates; q dot it is NaN. F2 keeps Inf because all input elements are finite. This violates the ruling never hide dense non-finite rows. It is inherited behavior deliberately retained, not a new F-to-F2 finite-result change. Device confirmation staged after blind seal.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry a NaN stored norm for non-finite computed norm as well as non-finite input, keeping rotation arithmetic unchanged; lead must resolve the conflict with the blanket finite-operand LF1 requirement by explicitly classifying intermediate overflow.
findings.prior_art: IEEE 754-2008 overflow/NaN propagation; TurboQuant (Zandieh et al. 2025) inherited norm/rotation. External literature unverified -- lead to check: TurboQuant normalized key norm overflow.
findings.status: source and constructed host arithmetic; GPU output not measured

findings.title: R3 census misses overflow in EB2b B*H guard and retains wrong extent exception contract
findings.argument: INDEX_CENSUS row apa_eb2b_run claims B*H is guarded, but B,H are signed int at line158 and B*H is evaluated in int in the guard. B=H=65536, KVH=8192, S=1 gives true product 2^32 (modular illustration 0), so comparison with INT_MAX/4 is not a valid range check; ISO C++ signed overflow is undefined. Subsequent int rows/grids inherit the overflow. Separately attention per-axis extent guards retained std::runtime_error generic dimensions text for out-of-int extents, while R3 requires ValueError naming the operand. These are incomplete R3 coverage, not newly introduced arithmetic.
findings.suggested_fix: Check B*H in int64 or with apa_spo_product before any int multiplication/allocation; use an operand-naming ValueError for out-of-range extents while preserving R4/F1 zero-extent contract as ruled.
findings.prior_art: ISO C++17 (2017) signed integer range/overflow; ordinary checked multiplication, no prior art known to me for the exact repair.
findings.status: source and host integer arithmetic; huge allocation not attempted
